title: P34 x P32 follow-up: ALiBi on 3 of the 8 heads (standard 3-head slopes 1/6.35, 1/40.3, 1/256) and NoPE on the other 5, instead of 115-fable's 4+4 split, in all six Peri-LN blocks (4.80M params)
description: Idea ID: P34 x P32 (hybrid ALiBi/NoPE heads), the complement of 119-claude's 5+3 split. The only edit is N_ALIBI 4 -> 3: heads 1-3 get ALiBi's standard 3-head slopes 2^(-8i/3) = 1/6.35, 1/40.3, 1/256 and heads 4-8 are NoPE; no new parameters or code. 119 showed that adding locality (a fifth, steeper 1/3.03 head) raised round-1 parse failures from 25/22/18% to 47/23/35% and cost 15 at eval, so removing locality (one fewer recency head, gentler steepest slope) should give cleaner 7+-line samples for expert iteration to build on.
hypothesis: The model is trained on proofs of <= 6 lines and scored at >= 7, so what matters is how its attention behaves at unseen distances. Recency-biased ALiBi heads fit cap-6 syntax but over-localise beyond it: 113 (all 8 heads ALiBi) had round-1 parse failures of 50/30/64%, 119 (5 ALiBi) 47/23/35%, 115 (4 ALiBi) 25/22/18%, and pretraining loss is indifferent (val 0.078-0.083 for all three), so the head split is chosen by extrapolation, not fit. Moving one more head to NoPE (5 position-free heads for content-addressed name lookup at any distance) and flattening the steepest remaining slope from 1/4 to 1/6.35 should continue that trend. Counter-evidence: all-NoPE (111, on the RoPE base) lost 40, so position does matter and the optimum may already be 4. Prediction if right: round-1 targets solved >= 722 mean (115: 718/756/691), round-1 parse failures <= 22% mean (115: 25/22/18%), eval ge10 >= 96 mean (115: 103/97/89), and a 3-seed mean above 631.33. Pretraining mechanics unchanged: 4,150-4,300 steps, final val loss 0.077-0.086, held-out greedy ~0.98. If NoPE heads cannot parse Lean syntax without a local head at 1/4, expect higher val loss (> 0.086), lower held-out greedy, and a worse round-1 start. Mechanism checks: round-1 targets solved and parse failures vs 115/119/113; r1->r4 gain vs 115's +384; eval ge10-12 and L* vs 115; steps and val loss vs 115.
expected_delta: -40 to +35 dev solves >= 7 vs 115-fable's 631.33 (central +3); round-1 targets solved 680-790, round-1 parse failures 14-30%; pretraining steps 4,150-4,300, final val loss 0.077-0.086; totals 1,450-2,000 s under the 2,400 s cap

arch.type: gpt (fork model.py) with Peri-LN blocks (LayerNorm on each branch output as well as its input) and hybrid attention heads: CHANGED head split, ALiBi on 3 heads and no positional signal on the other 5 (P34 x P32)
arch.pos: hybrid alibi/nope (CHANGED from 115's 4+4 split): no rotation of q/k in any block; additive per-head bias -slope_h * (query position - key position) on the scaled attention logits via SDPA attn_mask, slopes 2^(-8h/3) = 1/6.35, 1/40.3, 1/256 for heads 1..3 (Press et al. 2021 standard set for 3 heads) and 0 for heads 4..8 (NoPE heads: bias identically 0 except -inf for masked/future keys); same slope table in every block
arch.norm: layernorm (pre-LN on branch inputs + LayerNorm on attention and MLP branch outputs, Peri-LN, unchanged from 107)
arch.change: CHANGED vs 115-fable: only N_ALIBI (N_HEAD // 2 = 4 -> 3), so ALIBI_SLOPES = (2^-2.667, 2^-5.333, 2^-8, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0) = (0.1575, 0.0248, 0.0039, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0) instead of (1/4, 1/16, 1/64, 1/256, 0, 0, 0, 0). PeriLNBlock, ALiBiGPT (bias build, key positions in caches[0], mask handling), width, heads, depth, d_ff 1024, GELU, untied embedding/readout, ln_f, init, optimizer and schedule are byte-identical to 115. One fewer head has a recency prior and the steepest remaining slope is gentler (1/6.35 vs 1/4); five heads are position-free
arch.n_params_detail: identical to 115-fable, 113-fable and 107-claude: 4,800,000 (vocab 107); slopes buffer is not a parameter
arch.checkpoint_reconstruction: ALiBiGPT(vocab, 6, 256, 8) from this pretrain.py (its ALIBI_SLOPES = (2^-8/3, 2^-16/3, 2^-8, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0)), replace blocks with PeriLNBlock as in pretrain.py, then load state (same keys as 107/113/115). Loading these weights into 115's model (4+4 table) gives a different function. The live harness uses the returned model object through RL and eval
arch.kv_cache: unchanged code from 113/115/119 (caches[0] holds key positions; slope-0 heads get a zero bias plus the -inf mask); only the slope values differ, so 115's CPU cached-vs-full check (max abs logit diff 1.0e-6) covers the mechanism. Not re-run locally: the fork is not importable in this checkout

tokenizer.source: fork 51604b3 lean_tok.LeanTokenizer('lean_seq') via tokenizer.make_tokenizer; Lean 4 have-chain text, names n1..n64 numbered by first appearance

optimizer.name: split-QKV Muon (RMS-matched shape scale) with Polar Express orthogonalization on hidden matrices and the output readout head.weight throughout; continuous AdamW auxiliary (unchanged from 078-claude except the orthogonalization polynomial)

muon.precision: bf16 Newton-Schulz; fp32 momentum and parameters
muon.shape_scale: sqrt(max(rows, columns) / 256) per orthogonalized matrix (RMS-matched, unchanged from 115): Q/K/V each 1, attention output 1, fc1 (1024,256) 2, fc2 (256,1024) 2, head (107,256) 1
muon.schedule: same warmup/cosine fraction as AdamW; muon_lr = 0.01 * adam_lr / 0.001
muon.parameters: 24 hidden matrices (6 x qkv.weight (768,256) split into Q/K/V, proj (256,256), fc1 (1024,256), fc2 (256,1024)) plus head.weight
muon.license: MIT; full copyright and permission notice retained in pretrain.py
muon.qkv_split: After elementwise Nesterov momentum, reshape each qkv.weight update to (3,256,256) and orthogonalize the three roles separately; selected by the shape test size(0) == 3 * size(1), which only qkv (768,256) passes (unchanged from 115)
muon.coefficients_note: CHANGED: per-iteration Polar Express quintic coefficients (Amsel, Persson, Musco, Gower 2025; values as in modded-nanogpt, num_iters=5, safety factor 2e-2, cushion 2) replace Keller Jordan's fixed (3.4445, -4.7750, 2.0315) used five times. Same five iterations (two matmuls each on the Gram side plus one), same bf16 precision, same transpose/QKV-split/shape-scale handling.
muon.normalization: CHANGED: update / (Frobenius norm * 1.02 + 1e-6) (Polar Express safety factor) instead of update / (Frobenius norm + 1e-7)
muon.local_check: CPU check (float64 scalar map over sigma in [1e-3,1]): output singular values in [0.847,1.141] vs fixed quintic [0.471,1.202]; for sigma>=3e-3 [0.859,1.141] vs [0.682,1.202]. bf16 torch on random (256,256)/(1024,256)/(99,256) matrices: median singular value 0.94/0.95/1.02 vs 0.75/0.77/0.77, update RMS +14%/+14%/+19%.

optimizer.adamw_parameters: emb.weight, all projection biases and LayerNorm parameters (ln1, ln2, ln_attn_out, ln_mlp_out per block, and ln_f); head.weight and hidden matrices never enter pretraining AdamW
optimizer.decay_convention: unchanged from 070-claude: MUON_WD = 10 * WD * LR / MUON_LR = 0.1, so Muon per-step shrinkage lr*0.1 is ten times the auxiliary AdamW lr*0.1 (peak 1e-3 per step), applied to all 25 Muon matrices including head.weight; AdamW group decay wd 0.1 at lr 1e-3. Note: with output LayerNorms, Muon weight decay on proj/fc2 no longer shrinks a branch's residual write (the LayerNorm re-normalizes it); only the AdamW-decayed output gains set that scale
optimizer.clipping: joint global gradient norm 1.0 before both optimizers
optimizer.handoff: standard GPT weights only; pretraining optimizer states are discarded and frozen RL creates its own unchanged AdamW
optimizer.parameters: 24 hidden matrices (6 x qkv.weight (768,256) split into Q/K/V, proj (256,256), fc1 (1024,256), fc2 (256,1024)) plus head.weight

data.augmentation: random name start offset (lean_seq; same vectorised shift as abs over the n1..n64 name tokens)

config.init: Unchanged from 115-fable: fork default construction (normal 0.02 embedding/readout), blocks replaced by PeriLNBlocks and re-initialized with the fork _init (zero biases), then orthogonal_ on every 2D block parameter (gain 0.02*sqrt(max(rows, cols))); output LayerNorms gain 1, bias 0
